
== Japanese original printing source audit ==
Original Japanese source: encyclopedia p. 44, embedded JPEG xref 2069. <ref name="encyclopedia-172-full-source">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], pp. 44, 105. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive].</ref> Image SHA256 <code style="white-space:normal;overflow-wrap:anywhere">f0f09eb707e2374f31d5c6e5272dce1c22e93f4fceca45dccd3579af1985dcc6</code>. The original image is [[:File:Japanese-Premiere-Two-Player-Vader-Encyclopedia32-original.jpg]]. Printed wraps joined; ASCII digits, Latin letters, +, =, < and > normalized. Unique asterisk tracked separately; Tarkin lore underline retained. Original JPEG remains typography authority. Both originals prohibit deployment when two or more opposing unique characters are in play and call for a destiny draw after a losing battle, with a result greater than 4 causing an Imperial casualty. The original English says "one Imperial present"; the Japanese says 帝国軍の人員を一人 without a corresponding location restriction. The Japanese choice sentence says that the player may choose whom to lose. Printed absence is separate from rule-derived defaults and unknown data. No artist/translator credit is visible. Performer likeness attribution and Japanese GEMP implementation remain unresolved. The November 1998 tournament-language rule is dated context, not evidence of earlier or custom-format mechanics. No new rules or implementation equivalence is claimed.
